chunks: And from him, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The arrows are only directed at what the army/camp contains."

key_terms.السِّهَامُ: Arrows (metaphor for directed actions, judgments, or resources)
key_terms.الْعَسْكَرُ: The army or military camp (metaphor for the main body, community, or primary source)

ai.seo_question: What does the metaphor of arrows and the army mean in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of *al-Ziyadat* (supplementary rulings), this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) employs the metaphor of archery to establish the principle of targeting the primary source or collective entity, suggesting that legal judgments or resources should be directed at the main body rather than scattered. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on identifying the root cause (*asl*) in matters of liability and distribution, ensuring that efforts are not wasted on peripheral issues. The saying underscores the importance of precision in applying divine laws to the most significant targets within a community or case.
